taxonomic_note: Legacy Master Plant Pool name Chamaesyce prostrata is normalized to the current accepted Euphorbia name.
look_here_first: Start at a stem node. E. prostrata lies prostrate to decumbent but does not root at the nodes in the local Williamson County treatment; the upper-side stipules are free while the lower-side pair is fused across the node. Then confirm with fruit and seed: capsule hairs concentrate along the keels/toward the base, and mature seeds are sharply 4-angled with narrow transverse ridges.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local legacy Chamaesyce source; current Kew explicitly treats Chamaesyce prostrata as a synonym of accepted Euphorbia prostrata Aiton.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; broader exact-county reconciliation deferred.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum sandmat: opposite leaves, milky latex, tiny axillary cyathia, and a 3-lobed capsule; hair placement, stipules, capsule pubescence, and seed sculpture are high-value characters.
morphology_keys.growth_form: Annual with taproot; stems prostrate to decumbent, about 10–30 cm. In the local Williamson County treatment it is mat-forming but does not root at the nodes, unlike E. serpens.
morphology_keys.stems: Stems crisped-villous to nearly glabrous proximally; hairs are much more evident than in the essentially glabrous E. serpens.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite; blades broadly elliptic to elliptic-oblong, ovate-spatulate, or ovate, usually about 3–11(–15) × 3–6(–8) mm; base slightly asymmetric and rounded to slightly cordate/oblique; margins serrulate at least distally.
morphology_keys.stipules: Four stipules are associated with each opposite-leaf node: on the upper side of the stem the pair is free; on the lower side the pair is fused across the node. They are triangular-subulate/acuminate, under about 1 mm, often lacerate or fringed distally.
morphology_keys.cyathium: Cyathia solitary or in small cymose clusters; 4 reddish glands with rudimentary white-to-pink appendages.
morphology_keys.fruit: Capsule broadly ovoid, about 1.2–2 × 1.4–1.5 mm; crisped-villous along the keels and toward the base, often glabrous between the keels.
morphology_keys.seed: Seeds about 0.8–1.1 × 0.5–0.7 mm, sharply 4-angled in cross section, with several narrow, sharp, slightly irregular transverse ridges.
best_field_traits: prostrate/decumbent annual that does not root at nodes
upper-side stipules free; lower-side pair fused across the node
crisped-villous stems and lower leaf surfaces
serrulate leaves with slightly asymmetric bases
capsule hairs concentrated along keels and toward base
sharply 4-angled seeds with narrow transverse ridges
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Against E. serpens: check a node first—prostrata does not root there and has an upper-free/lower-fused stipule pattern; serpens frequently roots at nodes and has conspicuous fused deltate stipule scales. Then use fruit/seed: prostrata has hairy capsule keels and ridged seeds, while serpens has glabrous capsules and smooth seeds. Against E. villifera: prostrata is prostrate rather than usually erect/ascending and has hairy capsule keels; villifera has distinct filiform stipules, papillate surfaces, and glabrous capsules.

lookalike_matrix.Euphorbia serpens: strictly prostrate, frequently mat-forming and rooting at nodes

comparisons.key_distinctions: Start with the node: no node-rooting + upper-free/lower-fused stipules separates E. prostrata from the rooted, fused-scale mat of E. serpens. Then confirm with the hairy capsule keels and sharply ridged seed.
